subtitle: Cheese-stuffed poblanos in egg batter
verso: Battered the way God intended: fluffy and never greasy.
story: Roasted poblanos stuffed with cheese, wrapped in a fluffy egg batter, fried, and served in a thin tomato broth. They take patience. Grandma's are light and puffy, never greasy.

ingredients.title: Chiles
items: 6 large poblano chiles, flat and straight
12 oz queso Oaxaca, Chihuahua or asadero, cut in sticks

ingredients.title: Capeado (batter)
items: Oil for frying, about 1 inch deep

steps: Roast the poblanos directly over a gas flame (or under the broiler), turning, until blackened all over.
Put them in a bowl, cover with a plate or a plastic bag, and let them sweat 10 minutes.
Peel off the charred skin with your fingers. Don't rinse them, or you'll wash away the flavor. Cut a slit down one side and carefully pull out the seeds, leaving the stem on.
Stuff each chile with cheese and close the slit with a toothpick.
Make the caldillo: blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic, fry in the oil 5 minutes, add the broth and bay leaf, and simmer 10 minutes. It should be thin. Season.
Beat the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks. Beat in the yolks one at a time, just until mixed.
Heat the oil to 350°F. Dust each chile with flour, shake off the extra, and dip in the batter to coat.
Fry 2–3 minutes per side, spooning hot oil over the top, until golden. Drain on paper towels and pull out the toothpicks.
Set the chiles in the hot caldillo for a minute and serve with arroz rojo and beans.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. This one belongs to the open flame and the skillet.
tips: The flour is what makes the batter stick. Don't skip it.
Pick poblanos that are smooth and flat. They roast and peel evenly.

variations.name: Rellenos de Picadillo
variations.subtitle: Picadillo-stuffed chiles
variations.note: Stuffed with picadillo instead of cheese.

items: Batter and caldillo from the base

steps: Fill the chiles with picadillo instead of cheese.
Batter, fry and serve in caldillo as in the base.
